items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: the band around Chicago at that time was Erskine Tate, and he had all of the fine musicians... I stayed in Chicago and I left and after -- my mother died, I left -- I stayed there a little while, then I left and joined Roy again in New York.

ctx.x: Did they pay better than other places?

They were the only ones who paid, really. Yeah, they were the only ones who paid. But any way, this is the time that Ray had his band. After high school he had this -- most of the kids would go with Erskine Tate, or you know, some bands around there. But Ray formed his own small group. And really did very well, yes. So as I told you

then Grissom worked with us and then he left us and went to Lunsford. And this is when we got Scoops Carey to come with us, then he started playing with my mother and he took Dan's place. He couldn't sing but he played so beautifully, you know.
